answer: Sybil farms fail if entry is a scarce berth, not a free signup. Each new agent must claim one slot on a public jetty of bonded identities, posting a cedar stake that stays locked until peers attest real work across several epochs. Idle clones erode on a shared dune of decaying trust scores; when the score hits zero the berth frees and the stake burns. Cloning identities means paying a fresh stake and rebuilding attestations from scratch, so mass fakes cost more than they earn.
